patient.chief_complaint: Prolonged unresponsiveness with eye deviation, stiff posturing — initially diagnosed as stroke, now EEG shows GPDs, team unsure if NCSE
patient.history_present_illness: A 44-year-old Black female social worker presented to a community hospital with acute left gaze deviation, left-sided facial droop, and right-sided arm posturing. Initial NIHSS was 14. The stroke team activated and CT showed no hemorrhage, CTA showed left MCA M1 occlusion. tPA was administered and thrombectomy team was called. During the window for tPA administration, the neurology fellow noted the patient had a brief 30-second rhythmic jerking episode of the right arm that was attributed to post-ischemic cortical spreading depression. NIHSS decreased to 8 after tPA. The patient was transferred to your tertiary center for thrombectomy. On arrival, she is confused, continues with subtle right arm posturing, and has a left gaze preference. EEG was ordered because the floor team was concerned about whether right arm movements were seizure activity. An electroencephalographer notes the EEG shows 'generalized periodic discharges — could be post-tPA ischemic NCSE or metabolic changes.' The team is debating whether to treat as NCSE with benzodiazepines vs proceeding directly with thrombectomy.

medications.frequency: IV infusion completed 45 minutes ago at outside hospital

family_history: Mother: hypertension, stroke at 62. Father: diabetes. No family history of epilepsy.

social_history.note: Social worker. Single, lives alone. Non-smoker. Rare alcohol. No illicit drugs. Poorly medication-adherent per chart notes.

neurological_exam.mental_status: GCS 12 (E3V3M6). Confused, not following complex commands. Opens eyes to voice. Oriented to name only.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Left gaze deviation (conjugate gaze preference to left). Left facial droop, lower > upper. Pupils 3 mm bilaterally, equal and reactive. Blink reflex intact.
neurological_exam.motor: Right arm posturing (flexor) semi-rhythmically every 30-60 seconds. Left arm moves spontaneously. Right leg weaker than left on cursory exam. Post-tPA NIHSS 8.
neurological_exam.sensory: Unable to assess reliably due to altered consciousness.
neurological_exam.reflexes: Right upper and lower extremity hyperreflexia consistent with acute left hemispheric lesion. Right plantar extensor, left flexor.
neurological_exam.coordination: Not assessable due to confusion and right arm posturing.
neurological_exam.additional: Acute left MCA LVO post-tPA transfer. IIC/LPD pattern on EEG.

background.posterior_dominant_rhythm: Absent — replaced by continuous left hemisphere delta activity
background.anterior_rhythms: Generalized periodic discharges (GPDs) at 1.5-2 Hz maximal over left hemisphere with right-sided spread

findings.morphology: Sharp-wave morphology, periodic with occasional superimposed fast activity — ictal-interictal continuum (IIC) pattern

eeg.impression: This is an ABNORMAL EEG. 1. Lateralized periodic discharges (LPDs) — left hemisphere, maximal at F3, C3, T3; frequency 1.5–2 Hz; sharp-wave morphology with occasional superimposed fast activity (ictal-interictal continuum pattern). 2. Continuous left hemisphere delta activity replacing posterior dominant rhythm. This EEG was obtained under time-limited conditions; full characterization was not possible
eeg.limitations: Recording obtained under time-limited conditions; technical limitations apply.

findings.location: left MCA territory (insular cortex, lenticular nucleus)

ct.impression: Acute left MCA territory ischemic changes with early loss of gray-white differentiation in the insular cortex and lenticular nucleus. Hyperdense left M1 segment consistent with thrombus. No intracranial hemorrhage. No hemorrhagic transformation

background.posterior_dominant_rhythm: Continuous left hemisphere delta slowing, improved from prior
background.anterior_rhythms: Residual low-amplitude LPDs diminishing over the recording period

findings.frequency: Decreasing from 1.5 Hz to intermittent (<0.5 Hz) by end of recording

output.impression: This is an ABNORMAL EEG (follow-up recording). 1. Lateralized periodic discharges (LPDs) — left hemisphere — frequency decreasing from 1.5 Hz to intermittent (<0.5 Hz) by end of recording; attenuating morphology. 2. Continuous left hemisphere delta slowing present, reduced in amplitude compared with prior study. 3. No electrographic seizures identified on this recording. Comparison with prior study: LPD amplitude and frequency have decreased

findings.location: Left MCA core territory — insular cortex, lenticular nucleus, and mid-MCA convexity cortex

signal_characteristics.ADC: Corresponding ADC hypointensity — established infarct core

findings.mass_effect: Mild sulcal effacement over the left MCA territory

findings.location: Left MCA penumbra — superior and anterior convexity cortex

signal_characteristics.SWI: No haemorrhagic transformation identified — no GRE/SWI signal loss

output.impression: Left MCA territory infarct with DWI core approximately 40 mL, involving the insular cortex, lenticular nucleus, and mid-MCA convexity. Areas of milder DWI restriction in the superior and anterior convexity cortex may represent partial ischemic injury. No haemorrhagic transformation identified on susceptibility-weighted imaging. Geographic infarct distribution consistent with left MCA vascular territory

warnings: No pharmacokinetic or pharmacodynamic interaction between alteplase and levetiracetam. Levetiracetam does not affect fibrinolysis or coagulation. Safe to administer concurrently with or immediately after tPA.

output.query: acute stroke thrombectomy NCSE IIC LPDs management delay treatment

results.title: Seizures and status epilepticus in acute ischemic stroke: epidemiology and EEG characteristics
results.key_finding: Periodic discharges (LPDs, GPDs) are reported in a substantial proportion of large MCA territory ischemic strokes and are categorized as ictal-interictal continuum patterns. Their electrographic features, temporal relationship to stroke onset and reperfusion, and prognostic significance are described in the literature. Antiseizure medication use in this population and its effect on neurological outcomes have been examined in observational studies.

findings: Normal sinus rhythm. Normal axis and intervals. No acute ST-T changes.

csf.interpretation: Unremarkable CSF. Normal cell count, protein, and glucose.

findings: Structurally normal heart. No intracardiac thrombus or vegetation. No pericardial effusion.
No sustained arrhythmia. No pauses greater than 2 seconds. No AV block.

advanced_imaging.impression: No additional perfusion abnormality beyond established infarct territory.

specialized_test.impression: Study within normal limits. No residual proximal vascular occlusion.

ground_truth.primary_diagnosis: Acute left MCA ischemic stroke with post-ischemic lateralized periodic discharges on ictal-interictal continuum and post-reperfusion seizures

differential.key_features: LPDs on EEG can be NCSE per Salzburg criteria; coexistence with acute stroke established
Reperfusion can cause seizures and edema; ictal-interictal continuum on EEG

differential.diagnosis: Stroke mimic (Todd's paralysis from prior seizure)
differential.key_features: Initial diagnosis as stroke could be wrong if seizure preceded; MRI/CTA established ischemia
BP severely elevated; PRES on differential but MRI/CTA show MCA territory
tPA given; CT/MRI to assess for hemorrhagic transformation

optimal_actions.action: Continuous video-EEG — characterize LPDs and assess for NCSE in the ischemic hemisphere
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Left hemisphere LPDs at 1.5-2 Hz — ictal-interictal continuum requiring management

optimal_actions.action: Labs: CBC, CMP, glucose, AED level, lactate, ABG, coagulation (post-tPA), troponin, BNP, lipid panel, A1c, hypercoagulable workup as indicated
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Glucose 192 (hyperglycemia worsens outcome); coagulation status post-tPA

optimal_actions.action: Non-contrast head CT — assess for hemorrhagic transformation post-tPA
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Hyperdense MCA + early ischemic changes; no hemorrhagic transformation

optimal_actions.action: MRI brain + MRA — confirm territory and exclude additional pathology
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Confirmed left MCA territory infarct; post-thrombectomy reperfusion

optimal_actions.action: Drug-interaction check: tPA + AED + antiplatelet/anticoagulant timing
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Levetiracetam preferred (no bleeding interaction); avoid initiating anticoagulation prematurely after tPA

optimal_actions.action: Literature: post-stroke / post-reperfusion seizures + AED selection
optimal_actions.expected_finding: LEV preferred; treat NCSE if Salzburg criteria met; avoid prophylactic AED otherwise

optimal_actions.action: 12-lead ECG — assess for atrial fibrillation as embolic source
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Sinus rhythm or atrial fibrillation; impacts secondary prevention

optimal_actions.action: Carotid imaging for embolic source workup
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Carotid duplex or CTA for stenosis

useless_tools.rationale: Neuropsych battery cannot be performed acutely.
No infectious / autoimmune suspicion; LP not indicated.

sequence_constraints.reason: MRI/CT confirming no hemorrhagic transformation must precede any anticoagulation decision.

critical_actions: Continuous EEG to monitor LPDs / NCSE
Load IV levetiracetam if Salzburg criteria met or clear ictal evolution
Manage blood pressure per stroke guidelines (post-tPA target <180/105)
contraindicated_actions: Do NOT give prophylactic AEDs to stroke patients without evidence of seizures
Do NOT initiate anticoagulation prematurely after tPA
Do NOT delay neurology / stroke team involvement
Avoid initiating anticoagulation within 24h of tPA — bleeding risk; AED loading must respect this window.
key_reasoning_points: LPDs after stroke are on the ictal-interictal continuum; Salzburg criteria guide treatment
Post-reperfusion seizures can be brief or evolve to NCSE; close EEG monitoring is required
Anticoagulation initiation post-tPA must wait 24h with imaging confirming no hemorrhage

red_herrings.data_point: LPDs on EEG initially read as definite NCSE
red_herrings.intended_effect: Suggests aggressive AED escalation to anesthetic infusion
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: LPDs sit on the ictal-interictal continuum; Salzburg criteria + benzodiazepine response guide whether escalation is needed; not all LPDs require anesthetic infusion

red_herrings.intended_effect: Anchoring on stroke alone, missing the ictal-interictal component
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Stiff posturing can be from focal seizure activity (tonic component); EEG identifies the dual diagnosis

metadata.difficulty_rationale: 8 required + 2 recommended; concurrent acute MCA stroke and IIC LPDs; teaching is Salzburg criteria, post-tPA anticoagulation timing, prophylactic AED policy; 2 grounded red herrings.
